The lesions are irregular in shape, somewhat clustered, and appear sunken/flat rather than raised. The leaf is green otherwise. This matches Anthracnose description well (irregular brown to deep brown spots on leaves).

Now let me view one reference per class before deciding.
This Anthracnose reference shows a heavily affected yellowed/brown leaf. The test image looks different — the leaf is still green with discrete dark spots. Let me check the other classes.
Sooty Mould shows diffuse black sooty speckling across the entire leaf surface. The test image has discrete, larger brown lesions — not sooty. Not a match.
Powdery Mildew shows white powdery patches — clearly not the test image. Let me use my 4th view on a second Anthracnose reference to confirm.

This is a near-perfect match to the test image — a green mango leaf with discrete irregular dark brown/black lesions scattered across the surface. This is clearly Anthracnose.

**Reasoning summary:**
- Test image: green mango leaf with irregular dark brown lesions, flat/sunken appearance
- Anthracnose ref (Mango_Leaf_383): identical pattern — green leaf, discrete irregular dark brown spots
- Sooty Mould: diffuse sooty speckling, no discrete lesions
- Powdery Mildew: white powdery coating, no brown lesions
- Die Back: bark discoloration, twig withering — not leaf spots
